text:
nina: quick design check: suppression preview and channel badging felt confusing in the prototype. testers didn't realize suppressions applied to specific channels vs all channels.

alberto: noted. they saw the suppression pill and assumed it was global. we currently show the pill at top of the alert config, not per-channel.

sam: that's intentional for brevity, but we can make it clearer. maybe add a subtle per-channel indicator: when a suppression exists, show a small badge inside each channel row that says 'suppressed' with a tooltip.

marta: +1. UX should make the scope explicit. Suggestion: pill stays at top as summary, but add a channel-level badge with hover state "suppressed for 1h (overrides route)". Also when previewing notifications, show which channels would actually receive notifications given active suppressions.

alberto: implementation question: do we show suppressed channels as greyed out in the preview list or remove them? Testers were confused when preview showed fewer channels than configuration.

sam: prefer greying them with a strike-through icon and tooltip saying "suppressed by schedule". That communicates action without hiding config. Removing could seem like a bug.

a11y-bot: Accessibility note: do not rely on color alone to indicate suppression. Use both iconography and text. Ensure badges have aria-labels like "Suppressed for 1 hour" and are keyboard-focusable to reveal the tooltip or a visually-hidden description.

marta: copy idea for badge tooltip: "Suppressed until 3:45 PM — this channel will not receive alerts during the window." Short alt for badge: "Suppressed until 3:45 PM". Keep language active voice.

alberto: about the suppression editor: testers expected the preview toggle to reflect per-channel suppression toggles, but the preview only respected route-level settings. we need the preview to compute effective delivery per-channel, taking overrides into account.

sam: i'll update the preview logic to calculate effective recipients: start with route channels, apply SLO-level suppressions, then channel-level overrides. will include telemetry event `preview_effective_recipients` for debug.

a11y-bot: Ensure the preview changes are announced to assistive tech when it updates. Use role=region and update live region attributes or issue a polite aria-live summary like "Preview updated: 2 channels will receive notifications".

marta: design action items: 1) keep top-level suppression summary pill, 2) add per-channel suppression badge with tooltip and aria-label, 3) preview list shows greyed suppressed channels with accessible description, 4) preview logic to respect overrides and show effective recipients, 5) copy for badge/tooltip and accessible live summary.

nina: i'll update the Figma slices with the per-channel badge and two preview states (with and without suppressions) and post link.

sam: once Figma is up i'll implement and add unit tests for preview calc and aria-live messages.

amarta: thanks all — small follow-up: consider keyboard flow for editing a suppression schedule on a channel row; it should open a modal with focus trap and visible focus ring on the active input.

a11y-bot: reminder: modal must restore focus to the triggering element after close and errors must use role=status so screen readers announce them. Also verify contrast for greyed suppressed rows meets minimum ratio when relied on for comprehension.

marta: perfect. end thread — will post Figma link and two copy options for the badge later today.
